newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria says 1996 growth climbs to 3.25 percent.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria says 1996 growth climbs to 3.25 percent.

text.p: Nigeria's military government said on Saturday it achieved a growth rate of 3.25 percent in Gross Domestic Product compared to 2.20 percent the previous year.
"Most economic fundamentals moved in the right direction. Macro-economic stability was deepened and strengthened," military ruler General Sani Abacha said in the 1997 fiscal budget broadcast.
He did not give an estimated growth rate figure for 1997, but said policies would be aimed at: "Stimulation of growth and development of the Nigerian economy."
GDP growth for 1996 was realised from key sectors of the economy such as agriculture, petroleum and gas, Abacha said.
He said the rate of industrial capacity utilisation rose to 32.5 percent in 1996 from 29.3 percent in the previous year.
